factset.name: FactSet on X: Q3 earnings concentration

hormuz.label: Middle East war

facts.text: US and Israeli strikes on Iran on Feb 28 led to the near-closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries about a fifth of world oil.
Now: Houthi attacks threaten Saudi oil infrastructure, and the physical market is tight (Dated Brent traded above $120 in early October).

hormuz.say: The root shock is still the Middle East: Hormuz has been disrupted since February, and now Saudi infrastructure is under threat.
hormuz.keepReason: Disruption is ongoing; Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure in October keep it the root oil driver.

cheapai.label: Cheaper AI models

facts.text: Jul 17: Moonshot's Kimi K3 triggered a chip selloff that investors compared to the earlier 'DeepSeek moment'.
Oct 19: DeepSeek's latest model update pushed a Bloomberg gauge of Asian chipmakers to its lowest since July.
Sep 10: DeepSeek V4.1-Flash claimed much lower memory needs per task.

cheapai.say: Cheaper models keep raising the question of how many chips future AI really needs.

metacompute.label: Meta sells compute

facts.text: Meta said it would sell excess AI compute to outside customers. Meta's own shares rose about 9% on the news.
Micron fell 10.57% and AMD 6.89%, with about $200B erased from chip and cloud stocks.

metacompute.say: When one of the biggest buyers starts renting out spare capacity, the market reads it as possible overbuilding.
metacompute.keepReason: Origin of the overcapacity narrative that is still driving semis in October. Re-assess for retirement by 2026-11-15.

aicapex.label: AI capex boom

facts.text: Meta plans $125–145B of capital expenditure this year, mostly for AI infrastructure.
Hyperscaler capex plans are expected to keep bond issuance elevated into next year.

aicapex.say: AI capex is huge and increasingly debt-funded.

oil.label: Oil

facts.text: A five-month high, but below the 2026 intraday peak of $126.41 set on Apr 30.
Brent is up about 9% over the past month and about 78% year over year.
WTI spot was $101.08 on Oct 19; front-month futures traded near $98–99.

oil.say: Brent is back near $110, a five-month high but still below the April peak.

inflation.label: Inflation pressure

facts.text: University of Michigan year-ahead inflation expectations rose to 4.6% in September.
Canadian CPI is running near 3%, driven largely by gasoline.

inflation.say: Oil is keeping inflation sticky on both sides of the border.

issuance.label: Bond supply
issuance.value: Heavy Treasury and corporate issuance, incl. AI debt

facts.text: Macquarie's Thierry Wizman attributes this year's yield rise more to bond issuance than to inflation.
He expects hyperscaler capex plans to keep issuance elevated into next year.

issuance.say: Part of the yield move is plain supply: more bonds, including AI-related debt, need buyers.

overcap.label: Chip-demand doubt
overcap.value: Market fears AI compute is overbuilt

facts.text: Since July, investors have questioned the assumption that AI compute demand always exceeds supply.
This is the market's interpretation. Neither Meta nor DeepSeek said demand has peaked.

overcap.say: The scarcity story cracked: investors now ask whether chip demand has peaked.

fed.label: Fed
fed.value: First hike in over three years (September)

facts.text: The Fed raised rates in September for the first time in more than three years.
Markets are pricing further tightening; EY-Parthenon expects a December hike.

fed.say: The Fed has turned back to hiking, which is the big policy change this year.

y10.label: US 10-yr yield
y10.value: Peaked at 5.23% in late Sept, highest since 2007

facts.text: The 10-year started 2026 at 4.15%.
Drivers: inflation, Fed hikes, and heavy bond supply including AI-related borrowing.

y10.say: The 10-year hit about 5.2%, its highest since 2007.

realy.label: Real yields

facts.text: Real yields (after expected inflation) have risen on net since around the start of the Iran war in February.
So the rate move is not only inflation expectations; real borrowing costs rose too.

realy.say: Real yields are up, so this isn't only an inflation-expectations story.

boc.label: Bank of Canada

facts.text: The rate has been 2.25% for nearly a year; economists call Oct 28 a live meeting.
Employment fell by 68,300 in September; unemployment rose to 6.5%.
Hike odds reportedly swung from 20% to 80% after Governor Macklem's hawkish comments.

boc.say: The BoC is in a stagflation bind, and October 28 is a live meeting.

energy.label: Energy stocks

facts.text: Energy is the best-performing S&P sector this year (XLE +52.6% through Oct 16).
At the end of September energy was up 40.28% YTD, with Q3 expected earnings growth of 111.4%.

energy.say: Energy is the clear winner, up over 50% this year.

gold.label: Gold
gold.value: About $4,114, down ~5.3% over the past month

facts.text: Gold is slipping as oil-driven inflation concerns push investors to reassess the US rate outlook.
A stronger dollar and the 10-year near 5.14% add pressure.

gold.say: Gold is falling despite a war, which tells you real yields are in charge.

credit.label: High-yield credit

facts.text: HY spreads widened to their widest since April in early October, but the move has been orderly.
CCC-and-lower spreads are at 12.78%, the top of their record since Oct 2023.

credit.say: Credit is orderly overall, but the weakest borrowers are under real stress.

semis.label: Semis & tech
semis.value: SOX −11.41% in the week to Oct 16

facts.text: Chips fell eight sessions in a row; tech (XLK) was the worst sector that week.
In September the opposite happened: technology was the only sector that rose.

semis.say: Semis fell 11% in one week, eight straight down days.

cad.label: Canadian dollar
cad.value: USD/CAD hit ~1.43 earlier in October, then eased

facts.text: Rising expectations of a BoC hike are supporting the loonie.
CAD is also a commodity currency, so high oil helps it.

cad.say: Hike bets and oil are both supporting the loonie.

sbcorr.label: Stock–bond corr.

facts.text: The rolling 40-day S&P 500 vs US Aggregate correlation is at its most positive since 1999.
One estimate: +0.42 in 2026 through Aug 7, versus −0.36 over 2016–2021.
AQR: a positive correlation is a poor reason to swap bonds for more equity risk.

sbcorr.say: Bonds aren't hedging equities right now, so diversification has to come from somewhere else.

factor.label: Quality > momentum

facts.text: In Q3, US value, yield and quality moved ahead of momentum and high-volatility stocks.
Goldman's long-quality, short-momentum basket is up 55% in 2026 (mid-October).
Q2 was the exception, when AI euphoria put momentum on top.

factor.say: Quality and value are beating momentum as money gets expensive.

breadth.label: Equal vs cap weight

facts.text: Information technology was 39.7% of the S&P 500 in September.
More than half of S&P earnings growth comes from AI infrastructure; semis alone are over 40%.
Week of Oct 12–16: Nasdaq-100 −5.49% while the equal-weight S&P 500 finished up.
Year to date, equal weight and cap weight are roughly tied.

breadth.say: Owning the index is a concentrated AI bet: tech is about 40% of it.

edges.why: Lost Gulf supply and tanker risk lift crude.
Fuel and freight costs feed headline inflation and expectations.
Higher realized prices lift producer earnings.
Sticky inflation pushed the Fed into its first hike in over three years.
Oil keeps Canadian CPI near 3%, making Oct 28 a live meeting.
Hike expectations lift the whole curve.
Tightening raises rates after inflation, not only nominal rates.
Hyperscalers borrow to build data centres.
More bonds to absorb pushes yields up.
Higher borrowing costs make the same AI build-out more expensive to fund.
Gold pays no coupon, so higher real yields raise the cost of holding it.
Refinancing gets costlier, and the weakest borrowers feel it first.
Higher discount rates hit long-duration growth valuations.
When inflation drives rates, bonds and stocks fall together.
Low-debt, cash-rich firms hold up when money is expensive.
Stress in CCC credit rewards strong balance sheets.
Leaner models imply fewer chips and less memory per task.
A big buyer renting out spare capacity signals possible overbuilding.
Doubts about future chip demand hit semis and memory.
Tech weakness drags the cap-weighted index more than equal weight.
Momentum was crowded in AI winners, so its unwind favors quality.
Hike bets support the loonie.

chains.name: Why bonds stopped hedging
chains.script: The key portfolio issue is that bonds aren't hedging equities. The shock is oil: Hormuz disruption keeps Brent near $110, which keeps inflation sticky and pushed the Fed into a September hike. When inflation is what drives rates, a bad day for stocks is often a bad day for bonds too, so the stock-bond correlation turns positive. Nationwide notes the 40-day correlation is the most positive since 1999. I wouldn't abandon bonds. I'd shorten duration and add diversifiers with genuinely low equity beta, such as real assets and low-beta alternatives.

chains.name: Why gold falls in a war
chains.script: Gold falling during a war looks odd until you follow the chain. Oil lifts inflation, the Fed responds by tightening, and real yields rise. Gold pays no coupon, so a higher real yield raises the cost of holding it, and a stronger dollar adds pressure. That's why gold is down about 5% over the past month, near $4,100, even with the Middle East unresolved. In this regime, real rates beat the safe-haven story.

chains.name: The AI funding squeeze
chains.script: AI capex and rates are pulling against each other. Hyperscalers are borrowing heavily to build data centres, and that bond supply is one reason the 10-year hit 5.23%, its highest since 2007. But higher yields raise the cost of funding that same build-out and lower the value of long-duration growth stocks. So AI is both a cause of higher yields and a victim of them.

chains.name: The AI repricing
chains.script: The AI scarcity story cracked in July. Meta said it would rent out spare compute, which the market read as a sign of overbuilding, and cheaper Chinese models raised doubts about how many chips future AI needs. Semis fell over 11% in the week to October 16, and DeepSeek's update that weekend hit Asian chipmakers again. Money rotated toward equal weight and toward quality over momentum. With tech near 40% of the S&P, owning the index is a concentrated AI bet.

chains.name: Oil's winners and Canada's bind
chains.script: Oil cuts both ways for Canada. It lifts energy, the best S&P sector this year at about +52%, which helps an energy-heavy TSX. But it keeps Canadian inflation near 3% while jobs are falling, down 68,000 in September. That's a stagflation bind for the Bank of Canada, and October 28 is a live meeting. Hike bets are already supporting the loonie.

chains.name: Rotation to quality
chains.script: Expensive money is sorting companies by balance sheet. High-yield spreads are orderly overall, around 330 basis points, but CCC spreads are at their widest of this cycle, so leveraged borrowers feel higher rates first. In equities the same logic shows up as quality beating momentum: Goldman's long-quality, short-momentum basket is up about 55% this year.
